report.summary: Enumerated 7 public symbols and 18 claims in picker.py chunk 5. 11 claims kept, 7 uncheckable.
risks: doc_resolving loop | medium | Uses _field(ref, 'doc_path') which may be None; key becomes empty string '' then skipped. If doc_path is missing for all refs, doc_resolving stays empty and counted_per_doc = bool({}) = False, even if resolving==0. That triggers the note about missing per-document evidence. This is intentional per comment. | Confirm with a test where resolving==0 and report has no 'resolving' sequence.
window_lines dedup | low | Only the first occurrence of each line number is kept; if multiple broken refs point to same line, only one rewrite window is generated. This is fine.
gate_argv --ref | medium | Builds gate_argv from raw refs, not detail. If refs list is huge, argv may exceed OS limit. | Check max length of refs and consider batching.
spectral_row returns empty dict for absent module | low | Claim says 'absent means NOT MEASURED'. Correct per code.
island offset 30 vs 10 | low | test_only islands get 30, others 10. This is explicit.
unknown modules note | low | 'reported, not ranked' – note is appended but not used elsewhere. Correct.

claims.text: The corpus count alone is blind to a document that held no resolving reference: gutting it changes nothing corpus-wide, so the one move the denominator exists to catch would pass.
claims.why: The code computes doc_resolving per doc and uses counted_per_doc to detect this case. The note after the loop states exactly this.

claims.text: Measured by Minos.
claims.why: No reference to Minos in this chunk.

claims.text: A document with zero resolving references has no entry and a real count of 0 -- that is the case the second denominator exists for, so it must NOT be confused with 'we could not count'.
claims.why: doc_resolving dict has no entry for docs with zero; counted_per_doc is False if doc_resolving empty and resolving != 0.

claims.text: The distinction is whether the report carried the evidence sequence at all.
claims.why: counted_per_doc = bool(doc_resolving) or resolving == 0. If report had no 'resolving' key, doc_resolving stays empty and resolving is 0 (or None?), but code uses resolving from outer scope.

claims.text: Worst document first: most broken references is the biggest single correction available, and ties broken by path so the order is stable across runs rather than dependent on dict insertion.
claims.why: ranked = sorted(by_doc.items(), key=lambda kv: (-len(kv[1]), kv[0])) sorts by descending count then ascending path.

claims.text: A reference whose line number is missing or unparseable contributes no window rather than a guessed one: pointing an editor at the wrong lines is worse than letting it read the whole file.
claims.why: try: line_no = int(d['line']); except (TypeError, ValueError): continue. Missing/unparseable lines are skipped.

claims.text: Bounded so a document with a hundred broken references cannot move further than the band allows -- the gap to the next band is what keeps a measurement from silently reordering a human's stated priority.
claims.why: offset = min(40.0, 4.0 * len(refs)) caps at 40.

claims.text: WORDING IS LOAD-BEARING, measured on the first live loop run: the earlier phrasing of the guard sentence ... tripped change_risk's keyword escalation ... the classifier is deliberately blunt; the instruction is ours. So it states the same invariant in preserving verbs.
claims.why: Refers to change_risk and classifier outside this chunk.

claims.text: Every sentence, paragraph and file must SURVIVE the edit: the verifier counts the RESOLVING references before it judges the broken one, so a withdrawn claim lowers that count and fails the gate.
claims.why: Refers to gate behavior not in this chunk.

claims.text: Correcting the wording is the only accepted move -- a statement that quietly vanishes is treated as evidence destroyed, not as a fix.
claims.why: Refers to gate logic outside chunk.

claims.text: The first end-to-end attempt proved the default +/-40 fragment too expensive for an unattended loop: two HANDOFF windows asked the model to regenerate 1,352 words and were still running after four minutes.
claims.why: Refers to historical run data not in chunk.

claims.text: Docref is unusually precise -- the scan names the exact broken line -- so it requests only that line here. Live probes at +/-8 and +/-2 showed the bench reflowing 17->10 and 5->4 lines; exact-line windows make the splice invariant structural rather than aspirational.
claims.why: Refers to live probes and bench behavior outside chunk.

claims.text: Other callers that pass bare line numbers retain the provider's conservative DEFAULT_WINDOW_RADIUS unchanged.
claims.why: DEFAULT_WINDOW_RADIUS not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: Consumed via TaskSpec.metadata['picker_evidence']['rewrite_windows']; a consumer that ignores it gets today's full-file rewrite.
claims.why: TaskSpec not in this chunk.

claims.text: Drawn from `detail`, not `refs`, so the model is only pointed at lines the instruction actually named (both cap at 12).
claims.why: window_lines built from detail (capped at 12 refs).

claims.text: THE GATE IS THE RE-SCAN, NOT PYTEST. ``gate_paths=(doc,)`` became ``pytest docs/THAT.md``, which exits non-zero on a path pytest cannot collect -- every docref attempt failed its gate always, for a reason that had nothing to do with the fix.
claims.why: Refers to historical gate behavior outside chunk.

claims.text: ``--ref`` is built from ``refs``, not ``detail``: detail is capped at twelve for the instruction, and a fix that left reference #13 broken would otherwise pass. The raw text is the UNTRUNCATED one for the same reason detail truncates -- the gate refuses to judge a target it cannot find verbatim, so a 160-char copy would block.
claims.why: gate_argv uses refs directly (not detail). refs is the full list.

claims.text: These keys decorate a candidate the map already produced for reachability reasons; they never create one, never remove one, and never touch ``band_offset``.
claims.why: Function returns dict(row) if exists, else {}. No modification to candidates or band_offset.

claims.text: A module with no spectral row contributes no keys rather than zeroes -- absent means NOT MEASURED, and a zero here would read as a measurement that says something.
claims.why: Returns {} for missing module, not {'key': 0}.

claims.text: Islands and shims are deliberately DIFFERENT sources with different instructions. They look alike in a count ('unreached') and need opposite remedies -- an island is capability nobody can get to and usually wants wiring; a shim is indirection nobody uses and wants removing. Collapsing them into one 'unreached' bucket would hand a fixer the wrong verb.
claims.why: Code generates separate candidates with different source ('map_island' vs 'map_shim') and different instructions (via _map_island_instruction and _map_shim_instruction, not shown but implied).

claims.text: ``spectral`` is optional evidence enrichment from :func:`daedalus.mapping.spectral.spectral_evidence` -- structure measurements attached to the SAME modules, so a fixer can see whether the package around an island is tight or a pass-through. Omitted by default: the ranking, the bands and the candidate set are byte-identical with and without it. It is evidence, not a gate.
claims.why: Refers to daedalus.mapping.spectral.spectral_evidence outside chunk.

claims.text: Measured: an island whose tests already exist is cheap and safe to wire, because the behaviour is pinned before anything is moved. One with no importer at all is a research task wearing an engineering task's clothes -- same reasoning the inventory source uses.
claims.why: offset = 30.0 if is_test_only else 10.0. The comment explains the reasoning.

claims.text: Reported, never ranked: 'the engine could not classify this' is a finding about the MAP, and turning it into a work item would send a fixer to change code because a scanner was confused.
claims.why: unknown modules are only appended to notes, not added to candidates.

claims.text: Returns ``(candidates, notes)``. Pure: takes an already-parsed inventory so the ranking is testable against a fixture with no filesystem involved.
claims.why: Function signature shows it returns tuple of tuple and tuple. The body is not shown but the claim is about the interface.

observations.what: The doc_resolving loop uses _field(ref, 'doc_path') which may return None; if all refs have None doc_path, key becomes empty string and is skipped, leaving doc_resolving empty. Then counted_per_doc = bool({}) or (resolving == 0). If resolving != 0, counted_per_doc is False, triggering the note about missing per-document evidence. This matches the comment's intent.

The instruction string in docref candidate uses f-string with doc and len(refs). It also mentions 'the verifier counts the RESOLVING references before it judges the broken one' – this is a claim about external verifier not in chunk.
gate_argv includes --ref arguments for every ref in refs (untruncated). If refs list is very large, the command line may exceed OS limits. No batching is done.
The rewrite_windows dict is built from window_lines which deduplicates line numbers. If multiple broken refs point to the same line, only one window entry is generated.
map_candidates generates candidates for islands and shims separately. The island offset is 30 if test_only else 10. The shim offset is always 10.
The unknown modules are only added to notes, not to candidates. They are never ranked.
inventory_candidates function is defined but its body is not shown in this chunk (ends with docstring). It is a stub.
